source.basis: Operator facility page; structured facts only, no operator prose reproduced.

reading.body:
CloudHQ's LC8 campus in Ashburn is the largest published power block in Virginia data centers, at 756 MW of IT capacity.

The 756 MW is roughly 29 percent of the 2,563.4 MW published across the 29 Virginia facilities that disclose a megawatt figure at all. That share reflects disclosure as much as size, because 376 Virginia facilities are mapped and only 29 publish a number. The concentration of published capacity in a small minority of sites is the pattern, not an artifact of one operator.

The 850,000 square feet of technical space against 756 MW works out to about 889 watts per square foot, well above conventional enterprise density and consistent with power-hungry compute. Converting that load to racks requires an assumption the operator does not publish. At 40 kW per rack, 756 MW is roughly 18,900 racks. At 100 kW per rack, it is roughly 7,560 racks. Neither figure is CloudHQ's claim, and the accelerator count depends on chips per rack, which is also unpublished.

The specifications include no certifications, so nothing here indicates what the campus is qualified to host. What the data establishes is a single site with more published power than any other in Virginia, in the largest data center market in the country. The grid connection behind those 756 MW is the constraint that determines when, or whether, the capacity becomes usable.
